As data center development LAND USE accelerates, concerns regarding energy, water consumption, and land use impacts can raise concerns.

Chaves County can respond to the impacts of data centers by implementing proactive approaches such as: _ Require Conditional Use approvals for data centers requiring discretionary review of proposed plans ensuring compatibility with surrounding uses and evaluation of potential impacts on the community. _ Establish development standards for noise, setbacks, water use, energy demand, and emissions.

Support and encourage renewable energy infrastructure to power data centers. _ Implement Community Benefit Agreements, which can ensure commitments to reinvestment locally, infrastructure improvements, and environmental protections.

These can be codified as part of a Conditional Use Permit approval. _ Clearly identify data centers as a distinct use within the Chaves County Zoning Ordinance, rather than a lump it into a broad “utility” or “industrial” use category.

By providing clear guidance on data center development, Chaves County can ensure these projects support the community and align with quality-of-life goals. 4.5 LAND USE ISSUES DILAPIDATED BUILDINGS Participants in the Community Survey noted that the areas of Chaves County that most need visual improvement are residential and commercial buildings or properties.
LAND USE CONFLICTS The most recent significant land uses in Chaves County are renewable energy installations and data centers.

Utilizing the processes outlined for data centers above, Chaves County should provide clear guidance on renewable energy development and allow for public review of plans and identification of potential impacts. 4.6 ETZ COOPERATION There are a number of critical issues in the ETZ that Chaves County, the City of Roswell, and private land developers face if perimeter development is not properly managed.
